note.title: The four fundamental forces
steps: Name the four forces: gravitational, electromagnetic, strong nuclear and weak nuclear.
Link gravity with attraction over long distances.
Link electromagnetic force with interactions between charged particles.
Link strong nuclear force with holding the nucleus together.
Link weak nuclear force with radioactive decay such as beta decay.
note.answer: The four fundamental forces are gravitational, electromagnetic, strong nuclear and weak nuclear forces.

mcqs.stem: Which fundamental force binds protons and neutrons together in an atomic nucleus?
rationales: Gravitational force is the weakest fundamental force and does not bind the nucleus.
Electromagnetic force causes interactions between charged particles and repulsion between protons.
Strong nuclear force holds the nucleus together by binding its protons and neutrons.
Weak nuclear force is responsible for nuclear disintegration and beta decay.

mcqs.stem: The range of the strong nuclear force is of the order of:
rationales: The textbook gives the strong nuclear force a range of the order of 10⁻¹⁴ m.
10⁻¹⁷ m is the stated order of the weak nuclear force's range.
The strong nuclear force is short-range, not infinite-range.
10⁻⁴ m is not the range stated for the strong nuclear force.

options: It causes beta decay of a neutron
It attracts all objects over infinite distance
mcqs.stem: Which is an effect of the weak nuclear force?
rationales: The weak nuclear force executes beta decay, in which a neutron transforms into a proton.
The electromagnetic force binds atoms, molecules and crystals.
The strong nuclear force holds the atomic nucleus together.
Gravitational force acts over long distances and becomes weaker with distance.

options: It acts between electrically charged particles
It has a range of only 10⁻¹⁷ m
mcqs.stem: Which statement best describes electromagnetic force?
rationales: The textbook describes it as the force causing interaction between electrically charged particles.
It does not act only between neutrons; it concerns electrically charged particles.
The gravitational force is stated to be the weakest of the four forces.
The short-range force of order 10⁻¹⁷ m is the weak nuclear force.

options: It is a long-range force that extends to infinite distance
It acts only inside atomic nuclei
It is stronger than all the other forces

rationales: The section says gravity is long-range and extends to infinite distance, although it becomes weaker.
The strong nuclear force, not gravity, is associated with binding the nucleus.
The section says gravitational force is the weakest of the four forces.

rationales: The section names the unified force the electroweak force.
This is not the name given in the section for the unification.

examTips: This section is most naturally tested through short-answer questions asking for the four forces, their effects, or their ranges.
For a question about the strong nuclear force, state that it binds protons and neutrons in the nucleus and mention its short range of about 10⁻¹⁴ m.
For weak nuclear force, connect it to beta decay and radioactive decay; include its range, about 10⁻¹⁷ m, if asked.
For a comparison, keep the facts distinct: gravity is the weakest and long-range; strong and weak nuclear forces are short-range.
The section gives no worked example or exercise item specifically testing fundamental forces, so there is no section-specific worked calculation to reproduce.

explain.title: Four forces
explain.body:
There are four fundamental forces in nature. These are:

1. Gravitational force
2. Electromagnetic force
3. Strong nuclear force
4. Weak nuclear force

Every force comes under any of these forces. In other words, these four are the basic categories of force.

explain.title: Gravity and electromagnetic force
explain.body:
The gravitational force is the weakest one among all four forces. Being a long range force, it extends to infinite distance although it becomes weaker and weaker.

The electromagnetic force causes the interaction between electrically charged particles. Electrostatic and magnetic forces come under this category. These are long-range forces. Electromagnetic forces are stronger than gravitational and weak nuclear forces. This force causes all chemical reactions and binds together atoms, molecules and crystals.

explain.title: Strong nuclear force
explain.body: It holds the atomic nuclei together by binding the protons and neutrons in the nucleus overcoming repulsive electromagnetic force between positively charged protons. It is also a short-range force with the order of 10⁻¹⁴ m. If the distance between nucleons increases beyond this range, this force ceases to act.

explain.title: Weak nuclear force and unification
explain.body:
Weak nuclear force is responsible for the disintegration of a nucleus. For example, the weak nuclear force executes the β-decay (beta decay) of a neutron, in which a neutron transforms into a proton. In the process, a β-particle (electron) and an uncharged particle called antineutrino are emitted. In other words, we can say that due to weak nuclear force radioactive decay of atoms occurs. It is a short-range force of the order 10⁻¹⁷ m.

The section explains that the weak nuclear force and electromagnetic force can be modelled as two aspects of the same force, called the electroweak force.

mistakes: Do not mix up the roles of the strong and weak nuclear forces: the strong force binds the nucleus, while the weak force is responsible for its disintegration and beta decay.
Do not give the ranges in reverse: the strong nuclear force is of order 10⁻¹⁴ m and the weak nuclear force is of order 10⁻¹⁷ m.
Do not say gravity is the strongest force; the section specifically calls it the weakest of the four.
Do not describe electromagnetic force as acting only in nuclei; it acts between electrically charged particles and is long-range.
Do not omit that the antineutrino emitted in the described beta decay is uncharged.
